About

Full Professor of Applied Thermodynamics in the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Cassino and Southern Lazio (UNICAS), Italy.

Earned PhD in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Cassino in 1996, and from 2016 to 2019 held a tenured full professorship in the Department of Engineering at the University of Naples Parthenope before returning to Cassino.

"Airborne transmission is a recognized pathway of contagion — yet for decades it was rarely measured quantitatively at all."

My research sits at the meeting point of aerosol physics, environmental metrology and public health: how airborne particles — combustion soot, traffic emissions, exhaled respiratory droplets — form, disperse indoors and outdoors, and translate into exposure and disease risk. During the COVID-19 pandemic, his quanta-emission and infection-risk models, built with international collaborators, became widely used reference tools for assessing airborne transmission in shared indoor spaces.

Research focus

Six threads running through three decades of work on the air we share.

Aerosol science

Indoor & Personal Air Quality

Particle number concentration, size distribution and personal exposure assessment in homes, schools and vehicles.

Public health

Airborne Disease Transmission

Quanta emission-rate modelling and infection-risk assessment for SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory pathogens.

Metrology

Environmental Instrumentation

Design, calibration and validation of diffusion-charger and optical particle counters for field monitoring.

Atmospheric pollution

Combustion & PM Emissions

Emission factors and lung-dose/cancer-risk modelling for waste-to-energy plants, heating systems and traffic.

Radiological aerosols

Radon & Natural Radioactivity

Radon-progeny/particle interactions and radon emission from soil, springs and groundwater sources.

Building physics

Ventilation & Comfort

Ventilation strategies balancing energy efficiency, thermal comfort and healthy indoor air.

The aerosol world, illustrated

Schematic figures showing the particles and processes behind this research. They are simplified, not to scale, and not drawn from specific datasets.

Selected publications

Landmark papers, from personal exposure monitors to pandemic-era risk models.

2020
Buonanno, G., Stabile, L., Morawska, L. (2020).

Estimation of airborne viral emission: Quanta emission rate of SARS-CoV-2 for infection risk assessment

Environment International, 141, 105794

Formalized the quantitative estimation of viral quanta emissions as a function of vocal activity and respiratory energy expenditure, becoming the universal calculation basis for indoor predictive models adopted globally (ASHRAE, REHVA, CDC).

DOI 10.1016/j.envint.2020.105794
2021
Morawska, L., Allen, J., Bahnfleth, W., [...], Buonanno, G., [...], Yao, M. (2021)

A paradigm shift to combat indoor respiratory infection

Science, 372(6543), 689-691

A publication in a top-tier editorial journal (Science). It spearheaded the worldwide scientific and regulatory push to raise indoor air quality standards to match those of drinking water and food safety, directly influencing post-pandemic WHO advisory committees and international governmental guidelines.

DOI 10.1126/science.abg2025
2022
Morawska, L., Buonanno, G., Mikszewski, A., Stabile, L. (2022)

The physics of respiratory particle generation, fate in the air, and inhalation

Nature Reviews Physics, 4, 803–816

A foundational review with core group in Nature Reviews Physics. It demonstrates theoretical rigor in thermal-fluid dynamics and microphysics: breaking down the mechanisms of bronchiolar fluid-burst, droplet evaporation, airborne dispersion, and penetration into the respiratory tract.

DOI 10.1038/s42254-022-00506-7
2009
Buonanno, G., Morawska, L., Stabile, L. (2009)

Particle emission factors during cooking activities

Atmospheric Environment, 43(20), 3235-3242

A seminal lead-author historical paper, serving as a landmark in the characterization of domestic ultrafine aerosols. It introduced standardized number emission rates and factors for different cooking methods, which are used as essential input data in any indoor mass balance.

DOI 10.1016/j.atmosenv.2009.03.044
2014
Fuoco, F.C., Buonanno, G., Stabile, L., Vigo, P. (2014)

Influential parameters on particle concentration and size distribution in the mainstream of e-cigarettes

Environmental Pollution, 184, 523-529

One of the world's first independent quantitative studies on e-cigarette microphysics. It highlights how voltage, resistance, and liquid composition dictate the sub-micrometric particle size distribution and number density of inhaled and exhaled aerosols, pioneering the field of dosimetric toxicology for active and passive vapers.

DOI 10.1016/j.envpol.2013.10.010
2013
Buonanno, G., Marks, G.B., Morawska, L. (2013)

Health effects of daily airborne particle dose in children: Direct association between personal dose and respiratory health effects

Environmental Pollution, 180, 246-250

Marks the methodological shift from simple ambient stationary concentration (PM10/PM2.5) to calculating the actually deposited pulmonary dose (tracheobronchial and alveolar) using personal monitoring. It pioneeringly correlates number dose to spirometric responses and pediatric asthma exacerbations.

DOI 10.1016/j.envpol.2013.05.039
2022
Buonanno, G., Ricolfi, L., Morawska, L., Stabile, L. (2022)

Increasing ventilation reduces SARS-CoV-2 airborne transmission in schools: A retrospective cohort study in Italy's Marche region

Frontiers in Public Health, 10, 1087087

Retrospective cohort study on schools in the Marche region (>10,000 classrooms). It provided the international community and policymakers with the first large-scale empirical evidence of mechanical ventilation efficacy (risk reduction exceeding 80%), moving beyond purely theoretical modeling.

DOI 10.3389/fpubh.2022.1087087
2017
Stabile, L., Scungio, M., Buonanno, G., Arpino, F., Ficco, G. (2017)

Airborne particle emission of a commercial 3D printer: the effect of filament material and printing temperature

Indoor Air, 27(2), 398-408

Published in the flagship journal of the field (Indoor Air), this represents seminal work on the emerging risks of nanotechnologies and additive manufacturing in non-industrial enclosed environments (schools, offices, homes), analyzing the thermal effect of the extruder on ultrafine particle formation.

DOI 10.1111/ina.12310

DOI links open the article of record at its publisher. Publication and citation counts are approximate, drawn from public bibliometric profiles (Google Scholar, ResearchGate, Scopus) as of 2026.
